description: Extended teacher-reviewed assessment examples for the standalone handout. These do not add slides to the presentation.

slides.title: The teacher designs the evidence
slides.message: The goal, task and criterion must concern the same knowledge

comparison.label: Goal
comparison.text: Understand the roles of context, parameters and token selection.

comparison.label: Evidence
comparison.text: An explanation, commented diagram, justified prediction and correction.

comparison.label: Criteria
comparison.text: Concepts and relationships; process explanation; application and checking.

slides.decision: Assess what the learner can justify, alongside the assisted product.

slides.title: MagicSchool: draft a rubric
slides.message: The teacher provides goals, assignment and constraints
slides.prompt: Prepare a rubric for the attached assignment. Three criteria: concepts and relationships; process explanation; application and checking. Four levels with observable descriptors. Assess GenAI knowledge, without rewarding only polished prose or code. Distinguish the assisted product from the independent explanation.

steps.title: Open Rubric Generator
steps.text: Enter goals and assignment, without learner personal data.

steps.title: Generate a draft
steps.text: Check it against the textbook before using it.

slides.title: Review the rubric descriptors
slides.message: A constructed revision example, not automated assessment
body: Keep three criteria separate and apply the same rubric to the responses.

comparison.label: Too general
comparison.text: “Shows a good understanding of the topic”.

comparison.label: Observable
comparison.text: “Distinguishes parameters from context and explains why changing a prompt is not retraining”.

slides.decision: The rubric stays in the kit without Formative’s paid integrated rubric feature.

slides.title: Rubric: concepts and relationships

steps.title: 1 · Needs reconstruction
steps.text: Confuses training and inference, or treats probabilities as truth.

steps.title: 2 · Partial
steps.text: Names concepts, but incompletely relates parameters and context.

steps.title: 3 · Coherent
steps.text: Distinguishes phases and states correct relationships.

steps.title: 4 · Justified
steps.text: Justifies relationships and identifies conditions and limits in a new example.

slides.decision: Apply the criterion to meaning in the agreed response mode.

slides.title: Rubric: process explanation
slides.message: Criterion 2 · make the links between stages explicit

steps.title: 1 · Absent
steps.text: Repeats output without describing the stages.

steps.title: 2 · Fragmentary
steps.text: Describes some stages but leaves gaps or reversals.

steps.title: 3 · Ordered
steps.text: Connects input, tokens, processing, distribution and selection.

steps.title: 4 · Justified
steps.text: Explains the links and separates the diagram from observed data.

slides.decision: A commented diagram or oral explanation can reveal the same process.

slides.title: Rubric: application and checking

steps.title: 1 · Unjustified
steps.text: States a conclusion without a prediction or check.

steps.title: 2 · Incomplete
steps.text: Predicts, but changes multiple conditions or does not compare outcomes.

steps.title: 3 · Controlled
steps.text: Varies one condition, compares the outcome and corrects an error.

steps.title: 4 · Critical
steps.text: Justifies revision and recognises sampling, limitations and uncertainty.

slides.decision: Do not reward a lucky outcome from one generation.

slides.title: Prepare questions and expected answers
slides.message: The first question checks a fundamental distinction
body: Q1 · During ordinary inference, what changes when a new prompt is entered? A: original training data. B: calculation context. C: learned parameters.
Expected: B, with justification; a correct choice alone provides limited evidence.
slides.prompt: Generate five chapter-based questions: distinction, explanation, diagram, prediction and transfer. For each, provide the expected answer, a detectable misconception and the rubric criterion. Avoid questions answered by copying a definition.
slides.decision: A teacher-reviewed teaching example, not a validated test.

slides.title: Explanation and diagram completion

comparison.label: Q2 · Explain
comparison.text: Why does a token not always match a word? Expected: encoding may split words or represent other sequence elements.

comparison.label: Q3 · Complete a diagram
comparison.text: Complete text → tokens → model → distribution → selection. What repeats? Expected: the selected token joins the context and calculation continues.

slides.decision: Read correctness and explanation without requiring code.

slides.title: Prediction and transfer
slides.message: Questions 4 and 5 · apply a concept and recognise an error

comparison.label: Q4 · Predict
comparison.text: Same input and scores: what changes from T = 0.5 to T = 1.2? Expected: less concentrated probabilities, without a guarantee about one sampled token.

comparison.label: Q5 · Correct an error
comparison.text: “The most probable alternative will be true”. Refute using a new example. Expected: token plausibility differs from content truth.

slides.decision: Keep the initial prediction, test outcome and justified revision.

slides.title: Formative: set up the assessment
slides.message: One collection point, with clear instructions and available criteria

steps.title: Create the activity
steps.text: State the goal and when materials are allowed or chat must be closed.

steps.title: Add five questions
steps.text: Use multiple choice, open response and drawing in the Free plan.

steps.title: Prepare the review
steps.text: Key for Q1; teacher review for explanations and diagrams.

slides.decision: Use the standalone kit rubric; no premium integration is needed.

slides.title: Choose the format for the evidence
slides.message: Three response types, three opportunities to observe

comparison.label: Multiple choice + reason
comparison.text: Identify a distinction and inspect the reasoning.

comparison.label: Drawing + commentary
comparison.text: Make the sequence and relationships visible.

slides.decision: Integrated audio/video responses are paid features; agree alternatives when needed.

slides.title: Read three simulated responses
slides.message: Invented examples for discussing teacher judgement

comparison.label: Profile A · complete product
comparison.text: The diagram is complete, but the explanation says every prompt updates parameters.

comparison.label: Profile B · vocabulary present
comparison.text: Names tokens and probabilities, but omits the link between distribution and selection.

comparison.label: Profile C · coherent explanation
comparison.text: Distinguishes phases, justifies a prediction and recognises the limit of one generation.

slides.decision: Read differences criterion by criterion before summarising with a grade.

slides.title: Feedback that specifies the next action
slides.message: Teacher-written examples address the observed difficulty

comparison.label: For profile A
comparison.text: Revisit parameters versus context. Correct the arrow and explain why.

comparison.label: For profile B
comparison.text: Add the selection rule between distribution and token. Explain the link.

comparison.label: For profile C
comparison.text: Transfer your explanation to a new context and identify what remains uncertain.

slides.decision: Teacher-written feedback in the Free plan, followed by a new learner attempt.

slides.title: Activity: adapt an assessment
slides.message: Five minutes on your subject and an access barrier

steps.title: Choose a goal · 1 minute
steps.text: Name a concept you teach or study.

steps.title: Design evidence · 2 minutes
steps.text: Write a task and observable criterion, allowing AI to produce the initial product.

steps.title: Remove a barrier · 2 minutes
steps.text: Offer an equivalent access or response option; share the reason for your choice.

slides.decision: A reusable example with a coherent goal, evidence and support.
